Good to know

  • Change width and height to suit your column. The view fills whatever box it is given, down to about 280 pixels wide. Keep the title: a frame without one has no name for a screen reader.
  • loading="lazy" keeps the map from starting until a reader scrolls near it. A world or a crewed station starts a light version (about 2 MB); anything else starts the whole map, which is several megabytes.
  • The reader's camera is theirs: drag, scroll, pinch. Nothing in the frame takes a key from your page.
  • If your site sets a Content Security Policy, allow the frame with frame-src https://www.spaceradar.ai.
  • The full manual, with every parameter, is docs/EMBEDDING.md.

What the frame draws is modelled from public measurements: positions are worked out in the browser from published orbital elements and ephemerides, and the object's tag in the frame says how its numbers were worked out. Where a view is an artist's impression, it says so. The sources are listed on the Sources page and in CREDITS.md.
